features241.title: Combat built around the battlefield
features241.body: Full-body opponent art and a wider battlefield take center stage, with actions, weapon techniques, and the combat log arranged separately. Distinct effects for piercing, slashing, blunt, and mental attacks make each exchange easier to follow.
features241.alt: New combat illustration of an ogre carrying a huge club in a misty forest
features241.caption: Fog Border combat illustration · Ogre

features241.title: Decide what follows victory
features241.body: Regular Colosseum and Catfight Club matches now let you execute or spare a defeated opponent. Follow-up scenes reflect your choice and the match result, while practice matches follow a separate sparring conclusion.
features241.alt: Two fighters clash in the torchlit underground Catfight Club, surrounded by spectators
features241.caption: Catfight Club · The underground fighting pit

features241.title: Growth and prize money, together
features241.body: Victory results in the Colosseum and Catfight Club now include the prize announcement on the same screen. Rewards for ordinary Colosseum matches have also increased, making the results of a hard-fought win easier to review.

features241.title: Scenes that fit the character
features241.body: Isabella's tavern and recruitment scenes now match her current appearance. Egeya's combat art and weapon references have been revised, and match results and sparring dialogue now better fit the player character, slave, or assistant involved.

features241.title: Combat art for each setting
features241.body: Expanded combat and defeat illustrations across the Fog Border, arena, Catfight Club, and key event battles. Group enemies use group defeat scenes, and some monsters now look different at different growth stages. Base-game, Indie Patch, personal, and additional artwork have also been organized into a unified collection.

followups241: Chaotic Essence now prioritizes eligible negative traits. If none are available, it can randomly remove an ambiguous disposition instead. Clearly positive traits and protected entries are retained.
Buyer rumors now also consider whether a character can be traded and what standard buyers offer. When there is no suitable special recommendation, they can direct you to the Guild's purchasing agent.

groups240.title: Combat and Companions · Battle Experience and Personal Reputation
items: On Fog Border patrols, you can send one slave or assistant into battle first. If that companion is defeated, the player character can take over. Each combatant chooses equipment when entering the fight.

Switching combatants preserves the damage already dealt, defeated enemies, the enemies' remaining combat resources, and their special-move history. The switch itself does not give enemies an extra action.
Companions can also suffer death, injury, or changes to devotion and mood, depending on which combat resource runs out. Checking their condition and equipment before battle now matters more.
Improved ego and temperament growth for characters who personally win battles in the Fog Border. Expanded how battle experience and warrior backgrounds can lead to combat traits.

Witness accounts from the Fog Border, along with Rally and Catfight Club results, now contribute to a character's personal reputation. Rewards vary by activity, with adjustments for repeated victories.
Before choosing to fight in the Fog Border, dialogue can offer clues about an enemy's danger and combat strengths and weaknesses.

groups240.title: Traits and Training · Different Characters, Different Growth
items: Genius, Simpleton, and Ambitious bring more variety to learning speed and reactions to achievement, while Active and Prefers Rest distinguish attitudes toward work and rest.
Persistent and Distractible affect the results of repeated activities, while Petty and Generous change how characters remember unpleasant experiences.
Healthy Constitution and Frail affect combat resources and physical training. The fitness-growth benefits of Healthy Constitution have also been improved.
Berserker, Paladin, and Seasoned Warrior add distinct approaches to attack, defense, and staying power in battle. Brave and Cowardly also have stronger effects on combat morale.

Improved the discovery of Meiki (a rare intimate trait), the preservation of its discovery history, and its benefits for related skills and training. Fixed its connections to private-room activities and added a notice when it is first discovered.

Improved Peerless Beauty's special appearance evaluation and cosmetic-surgery outcomes, along with its trading, affinity, and reputation benefits. Its Korean display name is now consistent throughout the game.
Versatile contributes to the base value of a character trained across many fields. Its personal-reputation effect on first acquisition has also been improved.

Revised the names, effects, and lesson connections of traits involving sexual preferences and aversions, defiance and obedience, and speech. Slave Nature adds more variety to the dispositions of newly recruited characters.

Merged overlapping activity, rest, and attention-related dispositions, and resolved cases of incompatible traits appearing together. Current display names include Active, Prefers Rest, Attention Seeker, Strong Obedience, and Silver Tongue.
Open the full trait overview from the slave's or assistant's trait heading. The central information window brings traits and titles together, with the selected entry's description shown below.
The medical center now offers Constitution Improvement treatment to improve a character's constitution. The potion shop also offers Chaotic Essence for managing traits.
Adjusted base action points according to physical fitness and reduced the strain of overwork for muscular characters.

Improved Dull Cow's milk production, growth gains in certain specialist lessons for Genius characters, and some growth and production benefits from rare traits. Also aligned gains and messages across manual activities, automatic activities, and delayed reports.

groups240.title: Dialogue and Relationships · Replies Shaped by Personality and Recent Experience
items: Expanded assembled dialogue to cover the past, impressions, requests, desired activities, dislikes, current mood, and opinions of other characters.

Core lines and supporting remarks are combined according to personality, speech style, current relationships and emotions, and recent experiences. Recent wording repeats less often, while replies remain available even when there are few alternatives.
Reduced reactions that clash with a relationship and combinations of lines that contradict one another. Unique characters' stories and manually written backgrounds are preserved.
Long conversations about impressions now group related remarks and move topics to the appropriate questions. Pages break between complete sentences, with improved previous and next navigation.

When slaves and assistants discuss one another, the speaker and the subject are identified more clearly and the lines flow more naturally. Existing differences in affection and hostility are preserved.

Selectively revised origin stories, NPC introductions and titles, and text for the city, journal, bedroom, brothels, and red-light district to fit the current situation. Service prices and references to the current partner have also been aligned.

groups240.title: The World and Its Guides · Places, People, and Quests
items: Expanded missing or brief descriptions of regions, facilities, and NPCs, along with regional reputation, pharmacy products, quest guidance, and existing trait descriptions.

Facility descriptions now match the stage of a visit, such as the entrance or service screen. The introduction to cryo storage is separate from cell-use guidance, and the Catfight Club introduction is separate from the direct-duel explanation.
The grocery store and meat-trading screens keep stock information visible while showing location descriptions in the empty space below. Ongoing dialogue takes priority.

Corrected and translated combat, racing, and equipment descriptions; cleaning, nursing, and secretary lessons; everyday guidance; character names; and gallery headings. Also addressed missing choices, tooltips, input prompts, and duplicate descriptions.

groups240.title: Private Rooms and Storage · Easier Character Management
items: Choose and retain a separate diet for each private room. The whole diet row is now clickable, rather than only the small selection marker.

Private-room expansion limits now depend on the residence. Normal moves preserve existing rooms and occupants. Relocation during a financial crisis follows a separate process that includes disposing of assets.

Shared chores prioritize assignments to the slave and assistant. Private-room maids no longer duplicate those tasks or spend action points unnecessarily, and scenes show the character actually doing the work.

Private rooms apply their own rest and diet effects, with shared sleeping, diet, and portion-size effects turned off. Also improved room-specific character appearances, tutor-menu layout, navigation, and portrait browsing.
In cryo storage, find characters by the faces and names shown inside their cells and browse additional pages. Duplicate portraits and facility descriptions have also been tidied up.

groups240.title: Trading and Management · Assessing Value and Facing a Crisis
items: Improved the value and special trading benefits of Meiki, Peerless Beauty, and Versatile. Character value is also reflected in renegotiations with the dealer, additional bids at guild auctions, and bargaining with eligible customers.

Standardized general purchase appraisals around a character's current attributes, skills, obedience, and overall grade. Also revised sale-payment caps by transaction type and improved consistency between quotes and actual payments.
Local contacts can share buyer rumors suited to the characters you own. Recommendation browsing, return menus, and each contact's manner of speaking have also been refined.

When funds run short, a new crisis sequence lets you sell assets or seek the money yourself. Decorations, housing, facilities, and owned characters have separate disposal and settlement handling. Ongoing quests tied to a character who is actually sold off are marked as failed.
See your gold-coin balance on currency-exchange screens and in transaction results. Menu costs have been aligned with actual charges, and shop stock and potion-selection screens have been tidied up.

groups240.title: Screens and Artwork · From Status Checks to Cutscene Viewing
items: The monster's craving and satisfaction now appear as independent icons, separate from the assistant's personal status. Growth status remains available separately through tooltips and the existing guide.

Revised attribute, skill, and overall-grade labels and their reference tables. Also improved pregnancy-stage displays, the positions and sizes of slave and assistant status icons, and references to the correct character.

Refined trait-list fonts, colors, spacing, and the format of descriptions below. Also polished text on the main screen, private-room screens, status lists, combat logs, and weapon selection, along with character height in selection windows, borders, and confirmation buttons.
Removed the dedicated persistent Looseness icon while preserving its information in body details and all related effects.
Switch between original and alternate artwork and retain your selected image. Hiding the UI for cutscene viewing now also hides sale approval and rejection stamps.

Use Windows' Keep both files option to add an image with the same folder, filename, and extension. Alternate images numbered (2) through (4) are recognized without a separate program; other new numbers require separate registration.

Expanded and refreshed regional and facility backgrounds, large character artwork, portraits, variant images, and indie and personal alternate artwork. Also improved sequential scenes in the red-light district and salon, plus role outfits and profile support for some unique characters.
Restored equipment and storage descriptions and emoji, equipment-selection tooltips, and dedicated artwork. The art teacher now has a distinct lesson screen and icon.

Tidied up text, increase and decrease controls, navigation buttons, and trait-editing links in the cheat, player-character, and slave editors. Also improved adding and removing new traits through the in-game editors.

fixes.title: Combat Display, Weapons, and Group Scenes
items: Fixed missing or incorrect full-body opponent artwork in some event battles.
Corrected mismatches between enemy weapons, attack messages, and damage types, and restored missing weapon icons in the special skill menu.
Fixed individual defeat images overlapping the group victory scene, and corrected image references that gave different monster growth stages the same appearance.
Improved frame stability during combat effects, along with the alignment, colors, and line spacing of combat messages.

fixes.title: Catfight Club and Match Results
items: Fixed introductions that used a previous character's name instead of the current participant's name.
Refined the images and dialogue after execution or mercy choices, and the flow into sparring results for the player character, slave, and assistant.
Addressed mismatches between prize messages and actual payments, consolidated the separate prize-only page, and improved the return paths after results.
Fixed Catfight Club result images remaining over subsequent activity screens, including bathing, cooking, and cleaning.

fixes.title: Character Information, Private Rooms, and Daily Processing
items: Fixed some new traits remaining hidden when using trait-revealing magic or equipment.
Fixed ego growth from private room 2 being applied to a character in another room.
Improved Egeya's default image selection, full-body image paths for some unique characters, and character image links in Julia-related scenes.
Fixed guild-related daily notices appearing blank or extending outside the text panel.

fixes.title: Consignment, Inventory, and Accounting
items: Fixed failed returns caused by confusing an auction consignment character with another temporary candidate, along with some duplicate settlements.
Fixed some meat production quantities being omitted from the production summary in the accounts.
Improved Agrabah shop menus so unavailable products remain visible, making it easier to check why they cannot be purchased.
Tidied unnecessary headings and first-line spacing in character and location information panels, along with gold, special inventory, and some menu displays.

fixes.title: Lessons, Activities, and Combat Progression
items: Fixed blank screens after successful lessons, assistant lessons referring to slave calculations, and follow-up activities and return paths for advanced lessons.
Restored missing entry points in menus saved during earlier lessons and improved links to the assistant's lessons with an already hired partner.
Corrected companion action-point accounting in Fog Border battles, entry into some event battles, and duplicate Catfight Club win counts and participation restrictions.
Aligned rally entry requirements with the actual action-point cost, fixed races proceeding after entry was declined, and improved result branching for skill values outside the normal range.
Fixed some activities continuing to grant repeat rewards after their resources had been exhausted.

fixes.title: Household Management, Relationships, and Shops
items: Fixed private rooms 2 through 4 using room 1's diet settings, along with some lesson and milk-quantity links.
Fixed private-room maids duplicating household duties already assigned to someone else or wasting action points.
Corrected dialogue references to speakers, characters being assessed, and relationship targets, and refined repeated answers and some relationship and jealousy checks.
Fixed missing or duplicate payments in outings and reward activities, and improved price, balance, space, and purchase-cancellation checks for groceries, furnishings, and selected procedures.
Aligned black-market menu requirements with actual prices and prevented character creation and payment when funds or companion space were insufficient.

fixes.title: Characters, Events, and Existing Progress
items: Improved occupation modifiers, origin information, family relationships, saved backstories, and recognition of unique characters for some newly added characters.
Fixed rewards and purchases linking to the wrong character because of conflicting character numbers or incorrect registration data.
Fixed blank screens during some first meetings, progression on return visits, and the ability to purchase an already purchased character again.
Fixed event stages reverting and closing later choices, and progression stopping after certain equipment-wearing questions.
Improved startup, loading, and saved-menu refresh paths, and corrected paths that left a specific NPC scene displayed in another location.

fixes.title: Images, Icons, and Description Display
items: Corrected pregnancy indicators that read another role's confirmation state, combat companions' color portraits, and Edward's sepia portrait.
Fixed incorrect images in daily notices, role screens, and activity buttons, corrected some face and outfit references, and improved image-path compatibility for existing saves.
Fixed overlapping milk prices, funds, and stock quantities, missing shop icons, medicine selection ordering, and overflowing storage lists.
Tidied buyer-rumor menu placement and navigation links, missing choice translations, duplicate headings, and descriptions that did not match the current state.
Fixed edited Meiki status immediately reverting, along with some UI borders, word spacing, and line breaks.

other: Agrabah special inventory (in development): Added repeat purchases of the small 'Fresh Fruit' and 'Agrabah Wine' products, separate stored quantities, and purchase tooltips.
Updated the displayed game version to 2.4.1 and expanded the acknowledgments.
Refined MOB portrait frame categories, background colors, face areas, and borders.
Standardized the base dimensions of full-body combat and defeat images and organized location-specific background links.
Retained compatibility files at image paths referenced by some existing saves.
Tidied description heading formats, word spacing, currency notation, and some character encoding.
Expanded the image review checklist with combat sets and information on scene usage conditions and locations.
Improved image-replacement tools for size fitting, portrait face-area selection, and frame application.
Refined input ranges and list handling in the image-condition editor.
Removed duplicate listings of backup material with the same hash as other backgrounds from the image review checklist.
Organized source and exclusion records for original, personal, and additional resources, along with reproduction and review materials.
